item.title: What Albums Come Out in November 2026? Full Release Calendar
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: November 2026 album releases, week by week: Lil Baby, Skepta, Offset, Snoh Aalegra, Take That, GTA VI soundtrack and more. Updated every Friday.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Baby, Skepta, Offset, Westside Gunn, Snoh Aalegra, Take That and the GTA VI soundtrack: every confirmed November album, week by week.

November 2026 opens with Lil Baby's FRESH and Skepta's The Fork and Knife on Nov. 6, then hands the middle of the month to Offset, Westside Gunn and Snoh Aalegra on Nov. 13. Take That, the Grand Theft Auto VI soundtrack and Peter Gabriel carry the back half, and this calendar is refreshed every Friday as dates land or slip.

Friday, Nov. 6

The heaviest Friday of the month. Lil Baby locked in FRESH for the first Friday of the month, and Skepta answers from London with The Fork and Knife via Big Smoke/Epic. Pop gets Dove Cameron's FINAL GIRL and Shygirl's Swallow!, while Kings of Leon bring the rock.

  • Lil Baby — FRESH (rap)
  • Skepta — The Fork and Knife (UK rap/grime)
  • Dove Cameron — FINAL GIRL (pop)
  • Shygirl — Swallow! (UK club-pop)
  • Rex Orange County — Dream Fatigue (pop)
  • Blu DeTiger — N.Y. Baby (pop)
  • La Roux — Old Flames (synth-pop)
  • James Blunt — Airplane Mode (pop)
  • Kings of Leon — O My Beloved (rock)
  • Hatebreed — Fatal Paradox (metal)

Friday, Nov. 13

Rap owns the 13th. Offset pushed GMFU here after missing its October date, Westside Gunn drops Heelmatic through Mass Appeal, and Zelooperz lands on Earl Sweatshirt's Tan Cressida imprint. 2hollis jumps the queue with a Wednesday release through Interscope.

  • 2hollis — Pirouette (rap/electronic) — Wednesday, Nov. 11
  • Offset — GMFU (rap)
  • Westside Gunn — Heelmatic (rap)
  • Aesop Rock & Blockhead — Trouble Mountain (rap)
  • Zelooperz — Pin Breakers (rap)
  • Snoh Aalegra — Legendary Love (R&B)
  • Becky Hill — REBECCA (dance-pop)
  • Royal Blood — Dead Company (rock)
  • Jake Bugg — Alamo (rock)
  • U2 — Carnaval de Luz (rock)

Friday, Nov. 20 (plus Nov. 16 and 19)

Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, with Travis Scott, Future and Metro Boomin on board, drops on a Thursday alongside the game. Take That follow on Friday with their 10th studio album, and TXT open the week with a six-track EP.

  • TOMORROW X TOGETHER — PERFECT STORM (K-pop EP) — Monday, Nov. 16
  • Various Artists — Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album (soundtrack) — Thursday, Nov. 19
  • Take That — Dreamers (pop)
  • The Mars Volta — Lucro Sucio; Unfinished Business (alt-rock)
  • Trivium — Crown in the Grave (metal)
  • Lael Neale — As Killers Do (indie)

Friday, Nov. 27

Thanksgiving week runs thin on new studio albums and heavy on vinyl reissues, but Peter Gabriel's sprawling o\i on Real World is the headline.

  • Peter Gabriel — o\i (art rock)
  • Björk — Björk Orkestral with the Hamrahlíð Choir (orchestral)
  • Goo Goo Dolls — Borrowed (rock)
  • AJ McLean — Love, Sex & Money (pop)

Still waiting on a date

Teezo Touchdown's Casting Call is announced but undated. Gunna has said Splurge is close but has no date, Young Thug has teased an R&B album, and Don Toliver has pointed to 2026 for Nitrous. None has a confirmed November date yet.

Quick answers

What is the biggest rap album out in November 2026? Lil Baby's FRESH on Nov. 6, followed by Offset's GMFU on Nov. 13.

When does the GTA VI soundtrack come out? Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album is due Thursday, Nov. 19, the same day as the game.

Is there new R&B in November 2026? Yes. Snoh Aalegra's Legendary Love arrives Nov. 13 via Stem.

item.title: GENER8ION: The French Duo Who Cast Yung Lean in "STORM"
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: GENER8ION is Surkin and Romain Gavras. Here's how their Yung Lean film "STORM" came together, their past work and where to watch.
item.content:encoded:
Surkin and Romain Gavras turned a boarding-school short film into one of 2026's defining music videos.

GENER8ION is the audiovisual project of French producer Surkin and filmmaker Romain Gavras, two longtime friends who build music, film and installations around a shared vision of the near future. They are the team behind “STORM,” the two-part short film starring Yung Lean that became one of 2026’s most talked-about music videos.

Who is in GENER8ION?

Surkin, born Benoît Heitz, came up through France’s mid-2000s electronic scene and is tied to the French Touch 2.0 wave. Gavras, son of filmmaker Costa-Gavras, made his name directing videos for Justice, M.I.A., and Jay-Z and Kanye West before moving into features with Athena and Sacrifice. The pair have worked together for more than a decade, and their influences range from American rap and Japanese video games to Detroit techno.

Past work

The project surfaced publicly in 2021 with “Neo Surf,” featuring 070 Shake. Its debut album, Love & Tears, arrived in June 2026 with guests including 070 Shake, Adèle Castillon and Foals frontman Yannis Philippakis. GENER8ION also works in gallery spaces: Visions of 2034 ran at London’s 180 Studios over the summer, and GOD HATES SPACE, an immersive installation built around a 12-meter screen, opened at the Grand Palais during Art Basel Paris in October.

How “STORM” came together

“STORM” landed on April 24, 2026, as a double single, “STORM” and “STORM II,” released through Iconoclast Music. Gavras directed the roughly seven-and-a-half-minute film, Surkin handled creative direction and Damien Jalet choreographed it. The first half follows rebellion spreading through an all-boys British boarding school; the second turns euphoric, ending with uniformed students moving in synchronized waves on the school steps. YourInfoDaily covered the drop in “GENER8ION shares music video for STORM starring Yung Lean.”

Yung Lean’s role

The Swedish rapper, credited under his legal name Jonatan Leandoer, plays a brutish, magnetic bully who tears through the school and starts an informal fight club, with no dialogue. The FADER called the character “genuinely unnerving.” Gavras and Lean were already linked: Sacrifice marks his acting debut. It is a long way from early cuts like “Ghosttown,” his 2014 track with Travis Scott.

The film earned four nominations at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards, including Video of the Year and Best Direction, though it went home empty-handed. On the broadcast, Lean and GENER8ION restaged the climax with 66 dancers, Lean smashing a Moon Person and swapping the film’s cigarette for an ice cream cone.

Where to watch

The full two-part film premiered on YouTube on April 24, 2026, and remains there, with both halves in a single upload. For the wider world it belongs to, start with Love & Tears.

Who directed “STORM”? Romain Gavras, with choreography by Damien Jalet.

Is GENER8ION a band? It is a duo project from Surkin and Gavras spanning music, film and installations.

item.title: L.A. Singer Malcolm Todd Went From College Dropout to Radio City
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Malcolm Todd is the LA singer behind "Difficult Love" from Do That Again. His background, breakout songs, the track's meaning and tour news.
item.content:encoded:
The Pacific Palisades songwriter went from TikTok virality to Radio City Music Hall and a world tour.

Malcolm Todd is a Los Angeles singer, songwriter and producer who went from viral TikTok songs to a Columbia Records deal and a world tour. "Difficult Love" is a standout from his second album, Do That Again, released June 5, 2026.

Malcolm Todd's background

Born in 2003, Todd grew up in the Pacific Palisades neighborhood of Los Angeles and attended Palisades Charter High School. He was set to start at the University of Oregon but dropped out a week before classes began to do music full time. His first release, the 2022 EP Demos Before Prom, was co-written and produced with high school friend Charlie Ziman, who still drums in his live band.

How he broke through

The turn came in 2023, when "Art House" went viral on TikTok, followed by "Roommates." A Columbia executive took notice and signed him. In 2024 he released the Sweet Boy mixtape, featured on Omar Apollo's "Bleed" and opened the North American leg of Apollo's God Said No World Tour.

His self-titled debut album followed on April 4, 2025. Its single "Chest Pain (I Love)" became his first Billboard Hot 100 entry at No. 68 and went RIAA Platinum. Meanwhile "Earrings," a 2024 track, turned into a sleeper hit in 2026, reaching the top 40 in the US, UK, Ireland, Canada and Australia.

What "Difficult Love" is about

"Difficult Love" is not a breakup song. Todd sings about walking back into a relationship he already expects to go badly, treating the friction as part of the pull rather than a reason to leave. Songfacts sums it up neatly: love here "isn't blind so much as stubborn." Todd has not said who inspired it.

He co-wrote and co-produced the track with Ziman, touring keys and guitar player Jonah Cochran and Matthew Castellanos, whose credits include Steve Lacy's "Bad Habit." Like the rest of Do That Again, it was cut over six months between Electric Lady Studios in New York and Chaplin Recording Studios in Los Angeles. For a deeper read, see our breakdown, Malcolm Todd Knows It's Messy, and He's Choosing It Anyway on "Difficult Love".

Essential Malcolm Todd songs

Start with "Art House," the song that got him signed, then "Sweet Boy," "Chest Pain (I Love)" and "Earrings." From the new album, pair "Difficult Love" with "I Saw Your Face," a single he nearly abandoned before rescuing it on the final day of sessions.

Album and tour news

Do That Again runs 13 tracks on Columbia, and all 13 charted on Spotify's US chart in release week. The Do That Again Tour opened September 2 in Irving, Texas, played Radio City Music Hall in New York on September 22 and wrapped its North American leg at LA's Greek Theatre. Asia dates run from late November, Europe and the UK follow from February 2027, closing at London's O2 Academy Brixton, before Australia in May.

item.title: Akeem Ali: The Jackson, Mississippi Rapper Who Built a Career on Fabric
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Akeem Ali is a Jackson, Mississippi rapper behind "Mesh" and The Texture Tape series. His background, the song's meaning and his releases.
item.content:encoded:
From a viral Jackson alter ego to a fabric-themed tape series and a fall tour, here's the Mississippi MC's story.

Akeem Ali is a rapper and singer from Jackson, Mississippi, now based in Atlanta, best known for the viral 2020 alter ego Keemy Casanova and for his fabric-themed Texture Tape series. "Mesh," his June 2026 single, sits at No. 1 among his top songs on iHeartRadio, with an official video directed by Kevon Pryce.

Where Akeem Ali comes from

Ali grew up in Jackson and, by his own account to XXL, wrote his first rap at 11 before committing to music at 15. His first mixtape arrived in 2015, though he later pulled it from the internet. His path to the stage also ran through the military, a story he retold on The Morning Hustle this fall.

The breakthrough came with Keemy Casanova, a 1970s-styled mack persona he first posted on Instagram and Facebook in 2020. The clip spread fast, landing him a spot alongside Wild 'N Out comedians Karlous Miller and Chico Bean and turning a Southern lyricist into a viral character. He later joined Winners United, the independent label run by former NBA guard Lou Williams, who told REVOLT in 2022 that Ali would be the label's "North Star."

What "Mesh" is about

"Mesh" landed as a standalone single on June 1, 2026, released through Akeem Ali Music LLC and Winners United. It is a slow-burning love song about a tightly woven, committed relationship: two people promising loyalty, wanting each other badly and keeping the connection private. The title fits the Texture Tape concept, where songs are named after fabrics and materials.

The Kevon Pryce-directed video arrived in early August, and coverage of the visual places the song within The Texture Tape 3, the 11-track project released July 21, 2026. We broke down the visual in our earlier piece, Akeem Ali Releases Official Video for "Mesh".

His other releases

Ali's catalog runs deep for an independent artist. His debut project Rollin' came out in 2019, followed by D.E.A.D. (Do Em All Dirty) in 2021 and Roses Are Red But I'm Color Blind in 2023. In 2025 he launched the texture era with The Texture Tape, ten tracks titled after materials such as "Suede," "Cashmere" and "Egyptian Cotton," then followed with The Texture Tape 2 the same year.

The Texture Tape 3 leans into late-'80s and early-'90s R&B, with Ali naming Guy, Bobby Brown and New Edition as touchstones. Its emotional anchor is "Yarn," written in his car for his daughter. The 2026 run also includes the Hold Please EP and singles "Velvet," "Latex" and "Woman First." His projects have featured T.I., Big K.R.I.T. and Big Boi.

Where to follow Akeem Ali

His full catalog is on Apple Music and Spotify. He is on the road with The Texture Tour this fall, with dates booked across the Midwest, South and East Coast, including New York and an Atlanta stop at Center Stage on December 4.

item.title: Sekou: The Leicestershire Singer Who Became the BRITs' Youngest Nominee
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Sekou is a British-Ivorian singer from Leicestershire. His background, breakthrough, what "Does She Know" is about and which songs to hear first.
item.content:encoded:
The Leicestershire baritone with a BRIT nod, a Bieber feature and a KOKO headline date in London.

Sekou is Sekou Sylla, a British-Ivorian singer-songwriter from Leicestershire whose deep baritone and old-soul delivery have made him one of the UK's most closely watched young R&B voices. "Does She Know" is the lead single from his June 2026 mixtape In A World We Don't Belong Pt. 2, a song about realising someone was never who you thought they were.

Where he's from

Born in 2004 in Ashby-de-la-Zouch, Leicestershire, Sekou grew up singing gospel in church, where the musical director helped spark his interest in music. He has cited Whitney Houston, Amy Winehouse, Mariah Carey and Celine Dion among his influences, and the result is a sound that mixes contemporary soul with adult-contemporary balladry, gospel and touches of 80s funk.

How he broke through

He signed to Good Soldier Records at 16 after posting himself singing online, then spent two years developing before going public. His first single, "Better Man," debuted at Glastonbury 2022, where Arlo Parks handpicked him for the BBC Music Introducing stage. The 2023 EP Out of Mind followed on Island, and the momentum came fast: a Top 10 spot on BBC Radio 1's Sound of 2024 shortlist and a Rising Star nomination at the 2024 BRITs, making him the youngest BRIT nominee to date.

The London picture

London has been central to the rise. He has played Capital's Summertime Ball at Wembley Stadium, sold out a headline show at Outernet and appeared on Later… with Jools Holland. He played All Points East in August 2026 and headlines London's KOKO on December 14. His reach is widening too, with a featured spot on Justin Bieber's "Too Long" and an opening slot on Sam Smith's San Francisco residency.

What "Does She Know" is about

"Does She Know" opens In A World We Don't Belong Pt. 2, released June 26, 2026, alongside an official video. The song turns on betrayal and the slow discovery of a partner's true nature after being too swept up to see it. Sekou has framed it as a vulnerable record that reflects how much he grew over the past year. We broke down why the honesty on "Does She Know" hits so hard.

Songs to start with

Begin with "Better Man" and "Forgiving Myself" from his early run, then move to "Catching Bodies" and "Never Gunna Give You Up" from Pt. 1. On Pt. 2, pair "Does She Know" with "Dangerous Lover" and his cover of Fleetwood Mac's "Songbird."

What's next

Sekou is nominated for Best Newcomer at the 2026 MOBO Awards, and the KOKO date closes out a year that took him from US headline shows to festivals in Japan and France. A debut album has not been announced.

item.title: Teezo Touchdown: How a Beaumont, Texas Oddball Became Rap's Favorite Feature
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Teezo Touchdown is a Beaumont, Texas artist known for Tyler, Travis Scott and Drake features. Here is his story and what we know about Casting Call.
item.content:encoded:
From Beaumont to Tyler, Travis and Drake features, and a staged wedding that set up his second album.

Teezo Touchdown is Aaron Lashane Thomas, a rapper, singer and producer from Beaumont, Texas, best known for stealing scenes on records by Tyler, The Creator, Travis Scott and Drake. Now he is stepping back into the lead role with Casting Call, the follow-up to his 2023 debut, How Do You Sleep at Night?

Beaumont roots

Thomas learned to DJ and produce on his father's equipment and was posting songs to YouTube in high school under names like AyeTee and Teezo Suave. He settled on Teezo Touchdown in 2016, dropped the mixtapes The Example and Cover Boy in 2018, and still shoots most of his videos in Beaumont. The 2019 track "100 Drums" with Coop drew co-signs from Chance the Rapper and Trippie Redd, putting his genre-blurring sound on the radar.

The features that made him

The breakout came in 2021 on "RunItUp" from Tyler, The Creator's Call Me If You Get Lost, which went gold, and Teezo joined Tyler on tour. In 2023 he surfaced on Travis Scott's "Modern Jam" from Utopia, another gold record, and on "Amen" from Drake's For All the Dogs, which reached No. 15 on the Billboard Hot 100. He returned to Tyler's orbit on "Darling, I" from Chromakopia in 2024 and has also appeared alongside Lil Yachty, Don Toliver and Doja Cat. He keeps lending himself out, too, from Audrey Nuna's "Starving" onward.

How Do You Sleep at Night?

His debut album arrived on September 8, 2023, via Not Fit for Society and RCA Records. The 14-track set featured Janelle Monáe, Fousheé and Isaiah Rusk, and Drake publicly praised it as some of the best music he had heard. The rollout leaned into Teezo's theatrical streak, from "I'm Just a Fan" to the "Waist Snatched" video.

"Honeymoon Night" and the wedding that wasn't

The first single from Casting Call, "Honeymoon Night," landed in early October 2026 as a late-night R&B slow jam. Teezo paired it with a run of wedding-themed clips, including a bride fitting, a first-dance rehearsal and a pre-wedding photoshoot, which had fans asking whether he had actually gotten married. He had not. The videos credit a full cast, and the bride is played by Los Angeles makeup artist Jazzmin Oddie. The staged ceremony doubles as a neat setup for an album called Casting Call.

What we know about Casting Call

A 12-song tracklist surfaced in late August with a "dropping soon" tease, and "Honeymoon Night" is the first official single. No release date or guest features have been announced as of this writing. Our Casting Call release tracker will be updated the moment a date is confirmed.

Where is Teezo Touchdown from? Beaumont, Texas, where he still films most of his videos.

Did Teezo Touchdown get married? No. The "Honeymoon Night" wedding videos are a staged production with a credited cast.

When does Casting Call come out? No official release date has been announced yet.

item.title: How New Orleans, Louisiana Rapper Allay Earhart Turned a Katrina Photo of Himself Into the Cover of '2005'
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: New Orleans, Louisiana rapper Allay Earhart's album 2005 uses a Daily News photo of him at 9 outside the Superdome after Hurricane Katrina.
item.content:encoded:
Raised in the Calliope projects and now working at the New Orleans Public Library, Alvin Harris built 2005 around life before the storm.

New Orleans, Louisiana rapper Allay Earhart put his own childhood on the cover of his 2005 album. The image is a New York Daily News photo by Michael Appleton, taken outside the Superdome on Sept. 1, 2005, showing 9-year-old Alvin Harris, dehydrated, in his father's arms days after Hurricane Katrina.

The album uses a cropped version. The full image shows his father, Alvin "6th Ward Pook" Williams, carrying him past a row of armed National Guardsmen as the family tried to leave the city without being separated, the New Orleans Public Library reported.

A name with weight

Harris grew up in the Calliope projects. "I grew up in the Calliope projects, which is split down the middle by Earhart Boulevard," he told the library.

The stage name carries a second meaning. He took it from his cousin, Sadiki Navarre, who was murdered on that street in 2013.

The rapper who works at the library

Harris now works at the New Orleans Public Library, where a photo caption identifies him as a library associate. His path there ran through Crescent City Sounds, the library's free streaming platform for local music, which library associate Joshua Smith has led since its 2022 launch. Harris was a regular patron who noticed flyers for the service, and curators picked his 2022 album Great Habits, Great Heights in the platform's second submission round in 2023.

The library said it would celebrate 2005 with a release party at the Fillmore on Aug. 29, 2025, the 20th anniversary of the storm and his 29th birthday. "This album means a lot to me. It's all about living in New Orleans before Katrina, and how 2005 really changed everything," he told the library.

Beyond the booth

WWOZ's artist profile says he was raised by young teenage parents and faced hardships including homelessness, gun violence, and police brutality as a child, and that witnessing the success of Master P and No Limit Records inspired him to pursue music.

He runs VäKú L.L.C., a collective that supports local communities, and WWOZ says his VAKU brand co-sponsored the Nola Caribbean Fest and the Jerk Chicken Festival. In 2024, Mayor LaToya Cantrell gave him a Certificate of Recognition, according to WWOZ.

His stage history includes opening for Lil Wayne and Mac Phipps at the House of Blues and performing on the Coca-Cola stage at Essence Festival. He is a graduate of James Fauntleroy's 1500 Sound Academy, founded a music tech company to help independent artists, and is developing Montralize, an app meant to help artists earn sustainable income. He is also part of Metronome, the music business accelerator run by GNO Inc. and IdeaVillage. His songs have aired on WWOZ 90.7 FM, Q93, WHIV 102.3 and WBOK 1230 AM.

Where to listen and follow

His 2022 album Great Habits, Great Heights streams free on the New Orleans Public Library's Crescent City Sounds platform.

item.title: Robb Banks at Rolling Loud India 2026: Meet the Cloud-Rap Cult Hero Landing in Mumbai
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Robb Bank$ plays Rolling Loud India 2026 on Dec 13 in Mumbai. Here is his story, the songs to know and how to get tickets.
item.content:encoded:
A Tumblr-era mixtape star with a Naruto obsession, a Raider Klan past and more than a decade of releases.

Before streaming algorithms ran the show, Tumblr made rap stars. Robb Banks was one of them, and on December 13 he brings that cult-favorite energy to Rolling Loud India in Mumbai.

Who is Robb Banks?

Born Richard O'Neil Burrell in New York City in 1994 and raised in Broward County, Florida, Robb Banks (stylized Robb Bank$) first caught fire with his 2012 mixtape Calendars, which spread across Tumblr. That same year he was tied to the Raider Klan scene. In 2013 his father, reggae star Shaggy, confirmed the family connection, a story the rapper has never needed to lean on: his own catalog does the talking, per his Wikipedia profile.

The sound

Banks is a Southern-rooted, cloud-rap-leaning voice with an abrasive, brash delivery. He samples old-school R&B, pop culture and Japanese anime. Naruto is his favorite, and "Femto," his alias, is a nod to a character from the manga Berserk. His tag line, "I Think I Might Be Happy," comes from a scene in the U.S. version of Skins. Nerdy, moody and unmistakably his.

Songs and projects to know

  • "All the Way Live" and "On Me" (2013), from the Tha City mixtape
  • "Pressure" (2015), lead single from debut studio album Year of the Savage
  • "A Milli (4 M's)" (2018), a fan favorite
  • "Shootout" (2022, with Lil Uzi Vert) and "Lifted" (2022, with Trippie Redd), from the long-awaited Falconia era

He has also worked with Wifisfuneral, Chris Travis, Famous Dex and Tony Shhnow, and was part of the Members Only collective co-founded by XXXTentacion. His discography keeps growing: I Think I Might Be Happy (2024), Tha Leak 3 (2025) and 2026 releases Rich Badness and Unhappy - Side A.

Why catch the set

This is a rare India appearance for an artist who helped define the internet-born rap wave of the 2010s. Expect deep cuts for the day-ones and a crash course for everyone else. Not sure where to begin? Start with Calendars, jump to Year of the Savage, then queue the Uzi and Trippie collabs.

Locking in the date

Robb Banks plays Sunday, December 13, day two of Rolling Loud India 2026 in Mumbai. Tickets are on the District app, which offers a Reserve Now, Pay Later option (50% upfront, balance due by November 20, 2026), per Time Out India. The venue is still to be announced; full details at rollingloud.com/india.

item.title: Perfume Genius's 'Natural High' Opens 'The Lesson,' a Dance Piece Bound for Seattle, Washington
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Perfume Genius, raised near Seattle, Washington, shares 'Natural High' from The Lesson, a dance work with Kate Wallich bound for REDCAT, Barbican, Seattle.
item.content:encoded:
Mike Hadreas and choreographer Kate Wallich reunite for a Piano Teacher-inspired music-and-dance work, and the first song is a six-minute shape-shifter.

Perfume Genius, the art-pop project of Mike Hadreas, who was raised in the suburbs of Seattle, Washington, has a new song and a new stage show. "Natural High," shared Sept. 22, 2026, is the first release from The Lesson, a music-and-dance work he created with choreographer Kate Wallich.

The piece was commissioned by Seattle Theatre Group, and its 2027 tour ends April 9 at Seattle's 5th Avenue Theatre, according to Beats Per Minute.

A six-minute shape-shifter

Stereogum's Tom Breihan called the track "a six-minute epic that starts off as eerie ghost-folk," adding, "This is Perfume Genius operating at peak capacity." ArtistRack says it was released via Matador Records and runs 5:45, and Our Culture reports Fashion Club's Pascal Stevenson co-produced it.

Beats Per Minute hears sparse keyboard notes under Hadreas's fragile voice that build into waves of synths and close with a cosmic rave-up. Our Culture describes "Natural High" as a single from the work's score.

The Piano Teacher connection

The Lesson draws on Elfriede Jelinek's novel The Piano Teacher, per Stereogum and Beats Per Minute. It is the second collaboration between Hadreas and Wallich after 2019's The Sun Still Burns Here, the dance piece that led to his 2022 album Ugly Season. Stereogum says it will be performed live with Alan Wyffels and Tate Justus.

Wallich said, per Beats Per Minute, that she and Hadreas are drawn to "the same kinds of tensions and contradictions in the work we make." Hadreas has described his albums as "soundtracks to films that do not exist."

Where The Lesson goes in 2027

  • Feb. 6: North Adams, Massachusetts, MASS MoCA (work-in-progress showing)
  • Feb. 18–20 and 25–27: Los Angeles, REDCAT (world premiere)
  • March 4–6: New York, Baryshnikov Arts Center
  • March 17–18: Paris, Philharmonie de Paris
  • March 21: London, Barbican Centre
  • March 24: Utrecht, Birds of Paradise Festival
  • March 27: Dublin, National Concert Hall
  • April 1: Minneapolis, Liquid Music / Northrop
  • April 9: Seattle, The 5th Avenue Theatre

The stage work follows Glory, his March 2025 album, which earned a Best Album Cover nomination at the 2026 Grammys, per Wikipedia. Beggars Canada reported that Glory came out via Matador Records, with Hadreas re-teaming with producer Blake Mills. Hadreas was born in Des Moines, Iowa, and moved to the Seattle suburbs at age 6 or 7.

Where to listen and follow

"Natural High" is out via Matador Records, according to ArtistRack. Beats Per Minute points fans to perfumegenius.org/tour for tickets to The Lesson.

item.title: Why Points Nerds Keep Buying Alaska Atmos Points
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Why do frequent flyers keep buying Alaska Atmos Rewards points? Partner airlines, free stopovers, and no change fees. See the costs and the catches.
item.content:encoded:
It is not about flying Alaska. It is about who Alaska's points can put you on.

Disclosure: YourInfoDaily may earn a commission if you buy through links in this article. Offers change and are often targeted, so confirm the terms in your own account before buying.

Points enthusiasts keep buying Alaska Atmos Rewards points because they open seats on more than two dozen partner airlines, allow a free stopover, and can be canceled without a fee. People buy them to fly Japan Airlines, Qatar Airways, or Starlux, often in business class, for less than the cash fare.

That is the appeal. There are real catches too, and both are below.

What is Atmos Rewards?

Atmos Rewards is Alaska Airlines' loyalty program, formerly known as Mileage Plan, and it now covers Hawaiian Airlines as well. You do not have to live on the West Coast or fly Alaska to use it. Many members never do.

Reason 1: The partner list

One Mile at a Time lists the airlines you can book with Atmos points. They include American, British Airways, Cathay Pacific, Japan Airlines, Qantas, Qatar Airways, Finnair, Iberia, Aer Lingus, Korean Air, Fiji Airways, Air Tahiti Nui, Condor, Icelandair, Starlux, Hawaiian, Royal Air Maroc, and more.

For a touring artist or a founder with meetings abroad, that balance reaches Asia, Europe, the Middle East, the South Pacific, and most of the United States.

Reason 2: Business class at a known price

Published examples show why people do the math. Upgraded Points reported these one-way business class awards in February 2026, plus taxes and fees:

  • Japan Airlines, Tokyo to Chicago: 75,000 points.
  • Starlux Airlines, Phoenix to Taipei: 85,000 points.

During the most recent sale, One Mile at a Time put the best price at 1.88 cents per point. At that rate, 75,000 points cost about $1,410 and 85,000 cost about $1,598. Long-haul business class fares commonly run several times that. Award prices can change, so confirm current rates before you buy.

Reason 3: A free stopover

Atmos allows a stopover on partner awards at no extra points cost, even on a one-way ticket, according to One Mile at a Time. You can break a trip in a partner's hub city for days and continue on the same award. The exception is awards entirely within Asia.

For anyone combining a show, a meeting, and a few days off, that is two destinations for the price of one.

Reason 4: Low fees and no penalty for changing plans

Most partners do not add fuel surcharges to Atmos awards. One Mile at a Time names British Airways, Hainan, and Icelandair as exceptions.

Katie's Travel Tricks reports that Atmos award flights carry no change or cancellation fees, with points returned to your account and taxes refunded. The one cost that doesn't come back is a partner award booking fee, which the site lists at $20 per direction.

That flexibility helps buyers feel comfortable booking early. If a tour date moves, the points come home.

[Alaska Atmos Rewards Points - Check your Alaska Atmos Rewards points offer]

Reason 5: Sales come around often

The standard price is steep at 3.5 cents per point before tax. One Mile at a Time notes it used to be 2.75 cents. Almost nobody pays that. The program runs frequent bonuses:

  • July 30 to August 20, 2026: a bonus sale.
  • October 2 to October 19, 2026: a bonus of up to 100%, with reported tiers of 80% for 5,000 to 14,000 points, 90% for 15,000 to 29,000, and 100% for 30,000 to 100,000.

Offers are targeted. Some members reported seeing higher or lower bonuses than the published tiers, and some outside the United States reported none. Log in to see what your account shows.

Reason 6: Short flights are cheap too

It is not all first-class suites. Katie's Travel Tricks lists U.S. domestic awards from 4,500 points each way, and One Mile at a Time describes Atmos as good value for short and medium flights, especially on American. For a quick hop between tour stops, a small balance goes a long way.

The catches

  • The price is above the valuation. One Mile at a Time values an Atmos point at about 1.5 cents. Buying at 1.88 cents only makes sense for a redemption that beats that, which usually means premium cabins or expensive last-minute fares.
  • Partner seats are limited. You can only book what partners release. One Mile at a Time reports that American is pulling saver award space from partner programs within six days of departure.
  • There are limits. Non-elite members can buy up to 150,000 points per calendar year, not counting bonus points, with a maximum of 100,000 per transaction. The account must be at least 10 days old.
  • It is not airfare to your card. Points.com processes the sale, so it does not count as an airline purchase.
  • Programs change. Award charts can be revised. Buy for a trip you can book now.

How to buy like the people who do this well

  • Find the award seat first on Alaska's site.
  • Check the points price and the taxes.
  • Compare with the cash fare for the same flight.
  • Buy during a bonus, in an amount that hits the top tier if you need that many points.
  • Book as soon as the points arrive.

[Alaska Atmos Rewards Points - See your Atmos Rewards bonus and price out your award]

FAQ

Do I need to fly Alaska Airlines to use Atmos points?

No. Points can be redeemed on partner airlines around the world.

How much do Atmos points cost?

The standard price is 3.5 cents each before tax. With a 100% bonus, the cost is about 1.88 cents.

Do Atmos points expire?

Not as long as the account has activity at least once every 24 months.

Can I cancel an Atmos award ticket?

Yes. Reports indicate no change or cancellation fee, though a partner booking fee is not refunded.

item.content:encoded:
The Oklahoma-born, LA-based rapper who turned distortion and TikTok virality into a full album and a Rolling Loud slot.

Heavily distorted bass, bit-crushed drums and a crowd that goes feral: that is the 2Slimey experience, and it is coming to Rolling Loud India on Sunday, December 13. Here is the cheat sheet before you go.

The origin story

According to Wikipedia, 2Slimey is from Midwest City, Oklahoma, and now based in Los Angeles. He first released boom-bap as GGS, then discovered SoundCloud-era rap through Smokepurpp, Lil Pump and XXXTentacion. He began releasing as 2Slimey in 2021.

The sound

Complex describes a neo-jerk, hyperpop-influenced, bass-heavy sound with extreme distortion, and cites Playboi Carti and Yeat among his influences. Some listeners compare it to noise music more than conventional rap, and critics are split, which is part of the appeal.

Songs and records to know

  • "Shrimp" (March 2024), the TikTok-fueled breakout; Complex notes Lil Tecca used it in a skating video.
  • SsoMe (mixtape, November 2024).
  • High Anxiety (debut album, November 2025), a short, punchy project with "Meat" and "Live in Bass" among the standouts.
  • "Belly," made on a livestream with PlaqueBoyMax and included on the deluxe More Anxiety (February 2026).
  • TotalBass (EP, June 2026).

The 2026 run

This year has been a rapid ascent. He ranked 98th on Complex's "100 Hottest Rappers Right Now" list in April, performed at Rolling Loud on May 8, and played the Lyrical Lemonade Summer Smash in Chicago on June 13. Complex also reports a sold-out show at Dallas's 800-capacity Haltom Ballroom and a Lil Uzi Vert shout-out in a Dazed interview.

Why catch the set

Day two is stacked with Karan Aujla, Skepta, Seedhe Maut and ScHoolboy Q. 2Slimey is the curveball: short, brutal and built for the pit. If you want to be able to say you saw the internet's loudest new rapper before the room got bigger, this is your shot.

Festival info

Rolling Loud India runs December 12 and 13, 2026, in Mumbai; 2Slimey plays Sunday, December 13. Tickets start at ₹5,500 on the District app (the venue in Mumbai is still to be announced, and gates open around 3 PM per the District listing).

item.title: 5 Mistakes People Make Buying Hilton Honors Points
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Buying Hilton Honors points? Avoid five common mistakes, from trusting the headline bonus to booking the wrong room type, and keep the savings.
item.content:encoded:
The sale price is only half the story. These five errors turn a good deal into an expensive one.

Disclosure: YourInfoDaily may earn a commission if you buy through links in this article. Offers change and are often targeted, so confirm the terms in your own account before buying.

The five mistakes are trusting the headline bonus, booking the wrong room, ignoring the fifth night, paying with the wrong expectations about your card, and buying more points than you need. Each one is easy to avoid once you know it exists.

The context: One Mile at a Time reports a Hilton Honors bonus of up to 120% on purchased points from October 7 to November 21, 2026, which brings the cost as low as about 0.45 cents per point.

Mistake 1: Trusting the headline bonus

The phrase to notice is up to. Hilton's purchase bonuses are targeted, and different members may see different offers. A friend's 120% can be your 100% or less.

There is also a floor. The current bonus applies to purchases of at least 5,000 points in a single transaction. Buy fewer and you pay the standard one cent per point.

The fix: log in and read the offer attached to your own account. Do the math with your number, not the one in the headline.

Mistake 2: Pricing the wrong room

Hilton has no published award chart. The points price depends on the hotel, the date, and the room type. One Mile at a Time puts standard free nights at roughly 10,000 to 250,000 points, with premium rooms priced higher.

People often see a low points price in a search, buy points, and then find that the standard rooms are gone and only premium rooms remain at a much higher rate. The Points Guy notes that the price cap applies to a property's standard rate, not to every room.

The fix: search your exact dates and confirm that a standard room reward is available before you buy. Then book promptly once the points arrive.'

Mistake 3: Ignoring the fifth night

Members with Silver status or higher get the fifth night free on standard room reward stays, according to The Points Guy. The benefit applies to stays of up to 20 nights.

This cuts two ways:

  • If you have status and need five nights, you only need points for four. Buying five nights' worth wastes money.
  • If you need four nights and have status, check a fifth. An extra night can cost nothing.

Silver comes with some Hilton credit cards, and it is the lowest elite tier. If you don't have status, the fifth night free doesn't apply, so don't budget for it.

The fix: confirm your status in your account, then size the purchase around the nights you actually pay for.

[See the bonus on your Hilton Honors account.]

Mistake 4: Expecting hotel rewards on the purchase

Points purchases are processed by Points.com, not by Hilton. That has one practical effect: the charge does not count as hotel spending on a credit card, so you should not expect a hotel-category bonus on it.

One Mile at a Time suggests using a card with a minimum spending requirement, or one that earns well on everyday purchases.

The fix: pick the card for its general earning rate, and do not count on a hotel multiplier.

Mistake 5: Buying more than the trip needs

A big bonus makes it tempting to buy the maximum. During this promotion, the cap is 240,000 points before the bonus, up from the usual 160,000 per calendar year, and the top tier turns $2,400 into 528,000 points.

That is a lot of money parked in a currency Hilton controls. With no award chart, the company can raise what a night costs at any time. Points also earn nothing while they wait.

The value benchmarks are worth keeping in view. The Points Guy values a Hilton point at 0.4 cents and One Mile at a Time at 0.5 cents. At 0.45 cents, you are buying at about average value, which only pays off if your redemption is better than average.

The fix: buy what a specific booking requires, plus a small margin. Treat every purchase as final and check the refund terms before you pay.

A bonus mistake: spending points on the wrong things

Hilton lets you use points for rides, shopping, car rentals, and event credits. The Points Guy values those at around 0.2 cents per point. Airline transfers can be as poor as 10,000 points for 1,000 miles. If you paid 0.45 cents, each of those options loses more than half your money.

Hotel nights are where the value is. Keep buying points for rooms.

What a clean purchase looks like

  • You have dates and a hotel.
  • You have confirmed a standard room reward is available and noted the points price.
  • You know the cash price, including taxes.
  • You have multiplied the points by your own sale price and the points version is clearly cheaper.
  • You have checked the hotel's cancellation terms. Most Hilton award stays can be canceled free until a couple of days before arrival, but some properties are stricter.
  • You buy only what you need and book as soon as the points land.

Six checks, about ten minutes. That is the difference between a deal and a donation.

[Run the numbers on your own Hilton offer.]

FAQ

What is the minimum Hilton points purchase for the bonus?

The current promotion requires at least 5,000 points in one transaction.

Why is my Hilton bonus lower than advertised?

Offers are targeted by account. The advertised figure is the highest tier, not a guarantee.

Can I get the fifth night free with points I buy?

Yes, if you hold Silver status or higher and book a standard room reward stay of five nights or more.

Do Hilton points expire after I buy them?

Not as long as the account has activity at least once every 24 months. Buying points counts as activity.

item.title: How to Pick Wine for a Launch Party on a Budget
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Planning a launch or release party? Use this bottle math, a three-wine menu, and a sample Wine Express order for 40 guests under $400.
item.content:encoded:
The bottle math, the three-wine rule, and a sample order for 40 guests that clears free shipping.

Disclosure: YourInfoDaily may earn a commission if you buy through links in this article. This content is intended for readers 21 and over.

For a launch party, buy three wines, plan on roughly one glass per guest per hour, and order at least two weeks ahead. That covers an album release, a store opening, or a product launch without a sommelier or a blown budget.

Below is the math, a sample order, and the delivery details that trip up first-time hosts.

How much wine do you need?

A standard 750 ml bottle pours about five glasses. A common planning rule is one drink per guest per hour, with a little extra in the first hour.

  • Guests x hours = glasses. Forty guests for two hours is about 80 glasses.
  • Glasses / 5 = bottles. Eighty glasses is 16 bottles.
  • Add a 15% cushion. That brings you to 18 or 19 bottles.

If you are also serving beer, cocktails, or a strong non-alcoholic option, cut the wine count by a third. Not everyone drinks, and a good zero-proof choice is part of hosting well.

The three-wine rule

Too many choices slow the bar and leave you with half-empty bottles. Three wines cover nearly every guest:

  • One sparkling. It marks the occasion and photographs well.
  • One red. Medium to full body, nothing too tannic.
  • One white. Crisp and cold.

For an evening launch, split the order roughly 40% sparkling, 30% red, and 30% white. Go heavier on white and sparkling in warm weather or for a daytime event.

A sample order for 40 guests

These prices were listed at Wine Express on October 10, 2026. Several were sale prices, so confirm before ordering.

  • Sparkling: 8 bottles of Mionetto Prosecco Brut, Treviso DOC, at $15.75. Total: $126.00.
  • Red: 6 bottles of Fabio Cordella 2020 Il Castellano Primitivo, Salento, at $16.47 each. Total: $98.82.
  • White: 6 bottles from the under-$20 filter. Budget about $17 each, roughly $102.

That is 20 bottles for about $327 before tax, or a little over $8 per guest. At 12 or more bottles to one address, Wine Express ships ground free, so the delivery line should be zero.

Want one showpiece for the toast? A Belle Glos 2022 Pinot Noir magnum was listed at $85.95 and Moët & Chandon Brut Imperial at $52.95. One big bottle on the table does more for the room than upgrading every pour.

[Price out your party order at Wine Express.]

Where the savings come from

  • Free shipping at volume. Orders of $149 or more, or 12 or more bottles, ship ground free to one address.
  • Case discounts. Buy 12 or more bottles to get up to 15% off eligible wines. Sale-priced wines are excluded, so compare both ways.
  • The price filter. The catalog sorts by price band starting under $20. For a crowd, nobody needs a $50 pour.
  • Skipping the venue markup. Venues often charge well above retail per bottle. If yours allows outside alcohol, ask about the corkage fee and do the comparison.

The timeline

Wine Express says in-stock orders generally ship from New York within one to three days and arrive two to 14 business days after ordering, depending on location. Champagne needs three to five days of processing and cannot be expedited. Shipments may also be delayed due to extreme weather.

  • Three weeks out: confirm the venue's alcohol policy and headcount.
  • Two weeks out: place the order.
  • Delivery day: have an adult 21 or older ready to sign and show ID. A studio or office address works best.
  • Day before: chill whites and sparkling overnight.

Do not cut it close. If a box comes back unsigned, the sender pays return shipping and a 20% restocking fee, and your party has no wine.

Check these before you order

  • State rules. Wine Express does not ship to Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, Delaware, Hawaii, Kentucky, Michigan, Mississippi, North Dakota, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, or Puerto Rico.
  • Venue and permit rules. Some venues require their own bartenders, and selling tickets that include alcohol can trigger local permit requirements. Ask first.
  • Service basics. Check IDs, serve food, stock water, and line up rides. A launch should be remembered for the work.

What to do with leftovers

Keep unopened bottles. Store them in a cool, dark spot, and you'll have client gifts or a head start on the next event. Returns are limited to seven days and carry a 20% restocking fee, so plan to keep what you buy.

[Order early and let Wine Express deliver to your venue or studio.]

FAQ

How many bottles of wine do 50 guests need?

For a two-hour event with wine only, plan for about 20 bottles, plus a few spares. Reduce that if you are serving other drinks.

Is Prosecco fine instead of Champagne?

Yes. For a crowd, it is the budget-smart choice, and it ships faster than Champagne at Wine Express.

How far ahead should I order?

Two weeks is a safe margin given the two to 14 business day delivery window.

Can wine be delivered to a venue?

Yes, if the state is served and an adult 21 or older can sign. Confirm with the venue first.

Should I buy better wine for VIP guests?

Buy one or two special bottles for the toast or the green room and keep the main bar simple. Guests remember the moment the big bottle was opened, not the vintage in their second glass.

Nine bottles at nine price points, plus the delivery rules that decide whether the gift arrives at all.

The client gifts people remember look chosen, arrive on time, and get opened. A bottle with a story clears all three bars for less than most branded gift boxes, and the nine below cover budgets from a thank-you note to a closed deal.

All prices are as listed in the Wine Express gifting section on October 10, 2026. Most were shown as sale prices, so confirm before you order.

The nine bottles

1. Mionetto Prosecco Brut, Treviso DOC: $15.75

The volume play. With 30 names on the list, a recognizable Prosecco with a handwritten note beats a forgettable fruit basket. Listed with a 94-point score.

Bordeaux with nearly a decade of age, tied to one of Saint-Emilion's most famous estates. It reads as far more expensive than it is.

5. Nickel & Nickel 2023 Chardonnay, Truchard Vineyard, Carneros: $49.95

A single-vineyard Napa-area white from a name wine drinkers know. Safe for a client whose taste you cannot guess.

7. Belle Glos 2022 Pinot Noir, Clark & Telephone Vineyard, Magnum: $85.95

A magnum is a double-size bottle, and its size is a statement. This is the gift for a team, an office, or a client who hosts.

8. Laurent-Perrier Cuvée Rosé Brut Champagne, Gift Box: $92.95

Rose Champagne that arrives already boxed. Rated 95 points, it suits anniversaries of a working relationship and your most loyal accounts.

9. Louis Latour 2023 Corton-Charlemagne: $294.95

Grand Cru white Burgundy, rated 98 points. Reserve it for the 

one relationship that carried your year.

[Browse the full Wine Express gifting section.]

How to pick by relationship

  • New or small accounts: bottles 1 through 3. Keep it warm, not lavish.
  • Steady clients and referral sources: bottles 4 through 6. Recognizable names do the work.
  • Top accounts, partners, investors: bottles 7 through 9. Scale or rarity says what a card cannot.

If you want something between a bottle and a full case, the same section listed a WSET Level I in Wines Tasting Sampler at $149.99, a structured tasting set for the client who wants to learn.

The delivery rules that make or break a wine gift

Wine is not like sending a candle. Read these before you load a spreadsheet of addresses.

  • An adult must sign. Every delivery requires a signature and ID from someone 21 or older. Wine Express recommends a work address for client gifts.
  • Missed deliveries cost you. If the carrier cannot get a signature and the box is returned, the sender pays return shipping plus a 20% restocking fee.
  • Some states are off the list. Wine Express does not ship to Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, Delaware, Hawaii, Kentucky, Michigan, Mississippi, North Dakota, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, or Puerto Rico.
  • Champagne takes longer. Champagne orders need three to five days of processing and cannot be expedited.
  • Order early. In-stock wines typically arrive 2 to 14 business days after ordering, depending on location, and shipments can be delayed in extreme weather.

For a mid-December arrival, order before Thanksgiving week.

What a recipient sees

Wine Express leaves pricing out of gift packages, so the client sees the bottle and not the receipt. The company doesn't sell gift certificates, so every gift ships physically.

How to make shipping free

Ground shipping is free on orders of $149 or more, or 12 or more bottles, going to the same address. That helps when you are sending a case to one office. Gifts going to many different addresses are charged per shipment, as shown at checkout, so add that to your per-client budget.

One workaround: ship a case to yourself for free, then hand-deliver to local clients. A bottle handed over in person is remembered longer anyway.

A note on etiquette

Check a client's gift policy before sending anything over a modest amount. Some companies and most public agencies cap or ban gifts. And if you do not know whether someone drinks, ask a colleague or choose a different gift.

[Start your client list at Wine Express while holiday delivery windows are open.]

FAQ

How much should I spend on a client wine gift?

Match the relationship. The bottles range from $15.75 to $294.95, and most client gifts fall in the $25 to $95 range.

Can I include a note?

Add your gift message at checkout and confirm the options there. For wine club gifts, Wine Express says a handwritten card can be added by calling customer care.

Can I send wine to a client's home?

Yes, if the state is served and an adult 21 or older can sign. A work address is usually the safer choice.

Will the price show on the package?

No. Wine Express says pricing is not included in gift orders.

item.title: Zippy Raises $20 Million to Modernize the Most Overlooked Corner of the American Housing Market
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Zippy raises a $20M Series C from Saluda Grade to expand manufactured housing loans beyond 27 states and launch new products for communities and retailers.
item.content:encoded:
The manufactured-home lender's Series C from Saluda Grade follows more than $600 million in capital commitments secured this year.

Manufactured homes are one of the last truly affordable paths to owning a home in America. Financing them, however, has long been slow, paper-heavy and underserved by mainstream lenders. Zippy has just raised $20 million to change that.

The tech-enabled lender and loan servicer closed a Series C round with Saluda Grade as the sole investor, committing through its growth equity strategy, FinTech Global reported. Beyond capital, Saluda Grade will support Zippy on credit, capital markets, balance sheet management and product development.

A Lender Built for One Kind of Home

Founded in 2021, Zippy focuses exclusively on manufactured housing finance. It works with manufactured housing communities, retailers, dealers and wholesale partners, and has built its own loan origination platform covering digital applications, partner tools, underwriting, standardized paperwork and data infrastructure.

"Manufactured housing is already one of the most compelling affordable homeownership solutions in America, but it needs a financing system that is just as modern and efficient as the homes themselves," co-founder and CEO Ben Halliday said.

The Numbers Behind the Round

Zippy currently operates in 27 states. In 2026 alone, it has secured more than $600 million in capital commitments, the lending capacity that lets it fund loans at scale. The new equity gives the company room to keep growing that balance sheet while investing in technology.

"Zippy has built an impressive platform in one of the most overlooked sectors of housing finance," said John Stepp, head of ventures at Saluda Grade.

Why Manufactured Housing Is Having a Moment

With home prices and mortgage rates squeezing first-time buyers, manufactured homes offer a far lower entry price than site-built houses. Yet buyers often face higher rates and fewer lending options, in part because many manufactured homes are financed as personal property rather than traditional real estate. Lenders that can underwrite these loans efficiently stand to capture a market that big banks have largely ignored.

That gap is the opportunity Zippy is targeting: a vertical, software-driven lender that understands the economics of manufactured home communities and dealers better than generalist mortgage shops.

Saluda Grade's involvement is also strategic. The firm is known for its work in residential credit and capital markets, expertise that matters for a lender whose growth depends on reliably funding and selling loans. A sole-investor round from a specialist backer suggests conviction in Zippy's underwriting, not just its software.

For buyers, the promise is simple: faster approvals, clearer paperwork and fewer dead ends at the dealership or community office. For the industry, a well-capitalized digital lender could add competition to a segment where options have historically been thin.

What Comes Next

Zippy says the funding will help it expand beyond its current 27-state footprint, launch new loan products through community, retail and wholesale channels, and build out its technology and balance sheet capacity.

If it succeeds, Zippy could help make one of America's most affordable housing options easier to finance, and turn a long-neglected corner of lending into a serious fintech category.

item.description: London's Affinity Labs raises $2M pre-seed led by Fuel Ventures to co-found AI-powered software brands with creators, plus a £497K Innovate UK grant.
item.content:encoded:
The London startup co-founds apps with creators like Olivia Bowen, and says its portfolio revenue has been doubling month over month.

Creators have mastered attention. What most of them have not built is a business that runs without them on camera. London startup Affinity Labs wants to fix that by co-founding software companies with creators, and it just raised $2 million to scale the idea.

The pre-seed round was led by Fuel Ventures, with Antler co-investing, Tech.eu reported. Angel investors from Google DeepMind, Meta and Playfair VC joined, along with creator Marcello Ascani and Kyra CEO Devran Amaratunga Karaca. Affinity Labs also secured a £497,787 grant from Innovate UK, part of UK Research and Innovation.

Creators as Co-Founders

The model is simple to explain and hard to execute. Every product Affinity Labs launches is co-founded with a creator who brings an existing, engaged audience. Affinity Labs supplies the technology, product and operations needed to turn that audience into a paying software brand.

"Creators are the most underleveraged founders in the world," CEO Edoardo Ricci said. "Affinity Labs exists to be that infrastructure, we co-found every product with a leading creator."

Ricci runs the company alongside COO Ahmed Eltom and CTO Sunny Panchal.

AI Does the Heavy Lifting

What makes the approach scalable is a proprietary AI-powered development system that automates stages of the product lifecycle, from identifying software ideas and matching them with creator partners to building, operating and growing the products. That automation is what lets a small team run a portfolio rather than a single app.

Early Traction

Affinity Labs has launched four creator-led brands so far. Interior Design Clinic, built with Olivia Bowen, reached No. 34 in the App Store's Lifestyle category. Archives, built with Basel Ghazoghli, has more than 75,000 users and ranks among the top 200 Education apps. According to the company, portfolio revenue has averaged 100% month-over-month growth over the past three months, meaning it has roughly doubled each month.

Why It Matters

The creator economy has largely monetized through brand deals, merch and consumer products like beverages and cosmetics. Software is a different animal: higher margins, recurring revenue and products that can grow even when the creator takes a break. If AI lowers the cost of building apps far enough, a creator's audience may become the most valuable distribution channel a new software company can have.

What's Next

Affinity Labs will use the funding to expand its portfolio, support existing products and grow its product, growth and engineering teams. Part of the capital, including the Innovate UK grant, will go toward its AI product development technology.

The company plans to launch its first products with U.S. creators in late 2026 and has set an ambitious target of more than 200 creator-led software brands by 2030. For American influencers wondering what comes after the sponsorship era, that could make Affinity Labs a name worth knowing.

Source

Tech.eu — "Affinity Labs raises $2M to build AI-powered software brands with creators"

item.title: Elevation Capital Bets $10.5 Million That an AI-Powered Indian Studio Can Build Your Next Phone Game Obsession
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Spill Games raises $10.5M Series A led by Elevation Capital to scale its AI-led mobile game studio, Compass engine and casual puzzle titles worldwide.
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru's Spill Games, maker of Cozy Finds and Zen Math Crossword, lands a Series A roughly six months after its seed round.

The next puzzle game eating up your commute may be coming out of Bengaluru, and it may have been tested, tuned and scaled with help from AI. Spill Games, a two-year-old mobile studio, has raised $10.5 million (about ₹100 crore) in a Series A round led by Elevation Capital.

Existing investors Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital also joined the round, Inc42 reported. The raise comes roughly six months after Spill closed a $3.1 million seed round in April, a fast follow-on that signals strong early traction.

An AI-Led, Portfolio-Driven Studio

Founded in 2024 by Om Misra, Tapan Ranjan and Harsh Garg, Spill builds free-to-play casual, puzzle and hybrid-casual titles for a global audience. Its portfolio includes Cozy Finds, Sticker by Number, Zen Math Crossword, Bird Rescue Jam and Grill Master, monetized through advertising and in-app purchases.

"We started Spill because we love making and playing games," Misra told DealStreetAsia. The business model, however, is built on discipline rather than passion alone. Spill launches games quickly to test assumptions, then uses player feedback and in-game data to decide which titles deserve more investment and which get cut.

The Compass Engine

At the center of that process is Compass, Spill's in-house engine that brings together tools for analytics, player retention, monetization and live operations. Because the infrastructure is reused across games, the studio says it can shorten development and testing cycles, targeting speeds roughly four times faster than traditional approaches.

That speed matters in casual mobile gaming, where hits are unpredictable and user acquisition costs can sink a studio that bets too heavily on any single title.

Built in India, Played in America

Spill is part of a new wave of Indian studios building for players overseas. At the time of its seed round, the company said about half of its users came from the United States, followed by Brazil and Japan. It previously set goals of testing more than 20 prototypes within 18 months and launching five to ten profitable titles.

The timing is notable. India's government has banned real-money gaming, pushing investor attention toward studios that earn money from ads and in-app purchases instead of wagers. Spill sits squarely in that safer lane.

Where the Money Goes

Spill plans to use the new capital to scale its existing games, expand its development pipeline, strengthen the AI and technology capabilities of Compass, acquire users and selectively grow its team.

For Elevation Capital, one of India's most active early-stage firms, the bet is that a data-driven studio can turn hit-making from luck into a repeatable system. If Spill pulls that off, the American players already making up half its audience will be the ones who notice first.

Source

Inc42 — "Spill Games Raises $10.5 Mn To Scale AI-Led Mobile Gaming Studio"

item.title: 5 Things to Know Before You Buy Rapid Rewards Points
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Before you buy Southwest Rapid Rewards points, learn five facts on pricing, real value, Companion Pass rules, limits, and cancellations.
item.content:encoded:
Southwest's points work differently from every other airline's. Five facts decide whether buying them helps you.

Disclosure: YourInfoDaily may earn a commission if you buy through links in this article. Offers change and are often targeted, so confirm the terms in your own account before buying.

Before you buy Rapid Rewards points, know these five things: your discount is personal, a point is worth about 1.3 cents, bought points don't count toward the Companion Pass, the purchase isn't airfare to your card, and point bookings are unusually easy to cancel. Together, they tell you when buying helps and when it doesn't.

1. Your discount is not the same as everyone else's

Southwest's standard price is 3 cents per point. It discounts points regularly, but not equally. One Mile at a Time reported that during a sale running September 2 to October 2, 2026, different members were offered 35%, 45%, or 50% off. Award Travel Finder's tracker, updated October 9, 2026, listed a 50% discount through October 29.

On a purchase of 60,000 points, those tiers look like this:

  • 50% off: $900, or 1.5 cents per point.
  • 45% off: $990, or 1.65 cents per point.
  • 35% off: $1,170, or 1.95 cents per point.

The discount in that sale applied only to purchases of at least 3,000 points in one transaction.

What to do: log in and look at your own offer before you read anyone's verdict on the sale, including this one. A 50% offer and a 35% offer lead to different answers.

2. A point is worth about 1.3 cents, almost every time

With most airlines, a point's value swings widely, and experts hunt for sweet spots. Southwest is different. Frequent Miler explains that award prices depend on demand and the flight's cash price, rising and falling with the fare. Any seat for sale can be booked with points.

The result is predictable value. Frequent Miler's benchmark is 1.3 cents per point. One Mile at a Time estimates 1.1 to 1.5 cents.

That predictability works against buyers. No hidden jackpot makes points bought at 1.5 cents suddenly worth 4 cents. One Mile at a Time concludes that buying at 1.5 cents or more rarely makes sense, because points usually redeem for less.

What to do: treat buying as a way to complete a booking, not as a discount on travel.

3. Bought points do not count toward the Companion Pass

The Companion Pass lets a named companion fly with you for only the taxes. Frequent Miler requires 135,000 qualifying points in a calendar year.

Purchased points do not qualify. Neither do points transferred from another member, most bonus points, or points transferred in from hotel partners or Chase Ultimate Rewards. What does count: base points from paid flights, Southwest credit card spending, card welcome bonuses, and many partner activities.

What to do: if the pass is your target, put your money into paid flights and card spending. Buy points only for redemptions.

See the Rapid Rewards offer on your account.

4. There are limits, and your card sees a different merchant

According to One Mile at a Time, you can buy up to 60,000 points per day, with no annual limit. That is unusually open. Most programs cap purchases annually.

The sale is processed by Points.com, not by Southwest. Your credit card will not record it as an airline purchase, so do not expect an airfare bonus category to apply. One Mile at a Time suggests using a card with a minimum spending requirement or one with strong everyday rewards.

What to do: choose a card for its base earning rate, and buy only what your booking needs. The lack of an annual cap isn't a reason to stock up.

5. Points bookings are easy to undo, and points never expire

This is the best argument for holding Rapid Rewards points at all.

  • Cancellations. Frequent Miler notes that you can cancel award flights for no fee up to 10 minutes before departure, with points returned immediately. One Mile at a Time adds that a canceled cash ticket becomes a travel credit for a future flight, while redeposited points can be used for anyone.
  • Changes. If your flight price drops after you book, Frequent Miler says changing to a cheaper fare returns the difference in points.
  • Expiration. Rapid Rewards points do not expire, and no activity is needed to keep them. Closing your account forfeits them.

What to do: if your travel dates are uncertain, a points booking gives you a clean exit. After you book, check the price again periodically. If it falls, rebook and collect the difference.

Top up your Rapid Rewards balance.

So when should you buy?

  • Buy when you are a few thousand points short of a flight you are ready to book. A 3,000-point top-up at 50% off costs about $45.
  • Consider buying when your plans may change, and you value getting points back more than holding a travel credit.
  • Do not buy to pay for a whole trip at a 35% or 45% discount, to chase the Companion Pass, or because a sale is ending. Another sale will follow.

A quick self-check

  • What discount does my account show?
  • What is the cash fare, and what is the points price?
  • How many points am I actually missing?
  • If I cancel, would I rather hold points or a travel credit?

Two more notes. Southwest offers a Cash + Points option, which Frequent Miler says yields poor value per point. And free checked bags now depend on your fare, elite status, or a Southwest credit card, so include bag costs when you compare a Southwest fare with a competitor's.

FAQ

How much are Rapid Rewards points worth?

About 1.3 cents each by Frequent Miler's benchmark, with a typical range of 1.1 to 1.5 cents.

Is there a limit on how many Southwest points you can buy?

Up to 60,000 per day, with no annual cap.

Do Rapid Rewards points expire?

No.

Can I get a refund on points I buy?

Treat purchases as final and read the terms shown at checkout before you pay.

item.title: Vinci Pharmaceuticals Closes $8M Series A for Needle-Free Retinal Drug Implant
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Vinci Pharmaceuticals closed an $8M+ Series A led by Dynagrow Capital to advance EPIPLANT, a sustained-release episcleral implant for retinal disease, toward a 2027 trial.
item.content:encoded:
The New Jersey eye care company is preparing its EPIPLANT implant for a first-in-human trial in 2027 as an alternative to repeated eye injections.

Vinci Pharmaceuticals, a specialty eye care company based in Avon-by-the-Sea, New Jersey, has closed a Series A financing of more than $8 million to advance its EPIPLANT drug delivery platform. Dynagrow Capital led the round, with support from MintPharma Capital.

The raise follows $8.5 million in seed financing, bringing Vinci's total funding to more than $16.5 million.

What EPIPLANT Is

Many of the most common treatments for retinal diseases, including those affecting the macula, are delivered by injection directly into the eye, often every month or two. The treatment burden is heavy, and many patients stop treatment early, which can lead to vision loss.

EPIPLANT is designed to avoid that. It is a bioerodible implant placed on the outer surface of the eye, against the sclera, that releases medication to the retinal tissues over time without injections into the eye. The platform can currently deliver small-molecule drugs and is designed to work with a range of active ingredients.

The technology was developed in the lab of retina specialist Karl Csaky, MD, PhD, and is licensed from the Retina Foundation of the Southwest in Dallas. Vinci says it holds multiple granted patents and has completed preliminary preclinical testing.

How the Money Will Be Used

The proceeds will fund manufacturing, testing and release of its lead product, EPIPLANT VCI-002, under good manufacturing practice standards, as well as a planned Phase 1/2a first-in-human clinical trial in 2027.

Co-founder, chairman and CEO Philip A. Gioia described the financing as an important step toward that first human study. Dynagrow Capital managing director Sarah Hassan said a needle-free option could help reduce the high dropout rates caused by the burden of current treatment.

Why It Matters

Retinal diseases such as age-related macular degeneration and diabetic macular edema are among the leading causes of vision loss, and the drugs used to treat them form one of the largest markets in ophthalmology. Much of the industry's recent innovation has focused on making treatments last longer between injections.

Vinci is aiming further, removing the intraocular injection entirely. The approach still has to show in humans that it can deliver enough drug to the retina safely and consistently. With the Series A closed, the company has funding to manufacture clinical supply and bring EPIPLANT to its first patients.

Source

item.title: What Is Atlas Atomics? Ramaswamy's $1.9B Nuclear Bet
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Atlas Atomics is the stealth nuclear startup co-founded by Vivek Ramaswamy. It raised about $400M at a $1.9B valuation to build a heavy water reactor.
item.content:encoded:
The stealth company raised about $400M in a General Catalyst-led Series A to build a heavy water reactor that does not need enriched uranium.

Atlas Atomics, a stealth nuclear energy startup co-founded and backed by Vivek Ramaswamy, has raised about $400 million in a Series A round at a valuation of roughly $1.9 billion, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

General Catalyst is leading the round, with Andreessen Horowitz participating. Atlas Atomics, General Catalyst and a16z declined to comment, so the terms have not been confirmed by the company.

Who Is Behind Atlas Atomics

Ramaswamy, the entrepreneur and Ohio gubernatorial candidate, is a co-founder and backer. Day-to-day leadership sits with co-founder Kevin Gan, who spent more than 15 years investing in energy companies, most recently at hedge fund Millennium and before that at D.E. Shaw & Co.

The company's chief nuclear officer is Balendra Sutharshan, a former chief operating officer of Oak Ridge National Laboratory, the Department of Energy's largest science and energy lab and a central institution in American nuclear research. VentureTerminal lists the company in Columbus, Ohio.

The Technology

Atlas Atomics is developing an improved heavy water reactor. Unlike most reactors operating in the US, heavy water designs can run on natural uranium rather than enriched uranium. That matters because enrichment is expensive and global capacity is concentrated in a handful of suppliers, with Russia historically among the largest.

Avoiding enrichment could make Atlas's reactors cheaper to fuel and less exposed to supply bottlenecks. In a letter to Utah's Governor's Office of Energy Development, Gan said the technology aims to provide reliable power, expand production of medical and industrial isotopes and support nuclear fuel recycling.

Why It Matters

A $400 million Series A is one of the largest early-stage rounds in nuclear energy, and it arrives as demand for round-the-clock, carbon-free power climbs, driven largely by AI data centers. Tech companies have signed deals to restart old reactors and back new designs, and investors have followed with large checks into advanced nuclear startups.

Heavy water reactors are not new. Canada's CANDU fleet has run on the approach for decades. That track record could help with regulators, though any new design still faces a long licensing process with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. For Ohio, the company's ties to the state add to a growing presence in energy and advanced manufacturing investment.

Valuing a stealth company at nearly $2 billion before it has publicly shown a reactor is a large bet on its team. With a former Oak Ridge executive running the nuclear program and two of venture capital's biggest firms behind it, Atlas Atomics has the money and credibility to make its case.

Source

Bloomberg — "Ramaswamy Nuclear Startup Raises Funds at $1.9 Billion Value"

item.title: Can Light Beat Nvidia? Volantis Raises $88M for Photonic AI Chips
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Volantis raised an $88M Series A co-led by Lachy Groom and Abstract Ventures to build photonic AI inference systems that break the memory wall.
item.content:encoded:
Backed by Lachy Groom, Abstract Ventures and John Doerr, the San Francisco startup is using light to break the memory bottleneck in AI hardware.

Volantis, a San Francisco semiconductor company building AI inference systems that move data with light, has raised an $88 million Series A co-led by Lachy Groom and Abstract Ventures. The company announced the round as it works toward delivering its first integrated inference engines in 2027.

John Doerr, VXI Capital, Triatomic and Susa Ventures also invested, along with angel investors Dwarkesh Patel, Naveen Rao and Sholto Douglas.

WHAT VOLANTIS IS BUILDING

Volantis is going after what chip designers call the memory wall. As AI models grow, the limiting factor in running them is often not how fast a processor can compute but how quickly data can travel between the processor and memory. Electrical connections can only carry so much, and that ceiling restricts both model size and response speed.

The company's answer is photonics, using light in place of electrical signals to connect chips to memory. Its first system, called A-1, combines custom micro-VCSELs, a type of very small laser, with photonic interconnects designed specifically for chip-to-memory links.

Volantis says the architecture will let models exceeding 20 trillion parameters run at up to 10,000 tokens per second per user while lowering the cost of inference. Those are company targets for a system that has not yet shipped, and they would represent a substantial leap over what current hardware delivers.

THE TEAM BEHIND VOLANTIS

Volantis is led by CEO and co-founder Tapa Ghosh. The team includes veterans of NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom and Ayar Labs, with experience spanning CoWoS advanced packaging products, tunable VCSELs and silicon photonics systems.

"Today's hardware forces a tradeoff between running the largest models and running them fast. We started Volantis to eliminate that tradeoff," Ghosh said in the announcement.

HOW VOLANTIS WILL USE THE $88M

The funding will go toward developing and commercializing A-1, expanding the engineering team and preparing for customer deployments. The company is targeting 2027 for delivery of its first integrated inference engines.

An $88 million Series A is large by most standards but in line with what chip startups require. Designing, fabricating and packaging custom silicon and optics is capital intensive well before any revenue arrives.

WHY THE VOLANTIS FUNDING MATTERS

Most attention in AI hardware has centered on training, the process of building models. Inference, the work of running them for users, is where spending is shifting as AI products reach large audiences. Each query carries a cost, and that cost determines which products are viable.

Hardware that serves larger models faster and more cheaply would change that math. It is why investors continue to fund alternatives to conventional GPU systems, and why photonics, long confined to networking between servers, is now being pushed closer to the chip.

The investor list reflects that conviction. Doerr is one of Silicon Valley's best-known venture investors, Rao has founded AI chip companies of his own, and Patel and Douglas are closely followed voices in AI research circles.

Volantis still has to prove its design in production silicon. If A-1 performs as described, it would give AI developers a new way around one of the hardest constraints in the field.
